value.text: The prediction in the removed note was wrong and the reason matters. It said the next scheduled pm-ops release at 03:23 UTC would publish the fix. That run executed on 2026-08-10 at 04:59 UTC and FAILED, on a coverage gate reporting 99.89 percent branches for index.ts with no commit since the previous success. The cause was a test fixture pinned at 2026-08-03 that aged past the seven day throughput window overnight, making one branch unreachable. So no published pm-ops carries the .agents skip yet, and this task stays blocked until pm-ops pull request 41 lands and a release runs.

value.text: The previous symlink test (isMainInvocation resolves a symlinked entry path to the real module URL) passed argv[1] as the link and moduleUrl as the REAL path, which the old one-sided comparison pathToFileURL(realpathSync(entry)).href === moduleUrl also satisfied — it could not distinguish the fixed implementation from the broken one. Applied the missing canonicalization fix (both sides through realpathSync) and added a new test (canonicalizes a symlinked moduleUrl, as --preserve-symlinks produces) that puts the symlink in moduleUrl (pathToFileURL(link).href), which is what Node records in import.meta.url under --preserve-symlinks. Verified by measurement: reverting to the old one-sided comparison makes the new test fail (fail 1), restoring the canonicalization makes it pass (fail 0). The existing symlink test is retained because argv[1] arriving through an npm bin shim is a separate real case. Note: this repo's gate was on the old broken implementation (branch adopt-canonical-docstring-gate); the canonicalization fix was applied as part of this change.
